PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. CPU
   B. Monitor
   C. Keyboard
   D. Speaker

2. When learning Computer Concepts, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Computer Concepts.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Computer Concepts.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Computer Concepts.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Computer Concepts.

3. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Ignore burnt cables
   B. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   C. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   D. Overload every socket

4. When learning ICT Tools in Communication, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for ICT Tools in Communication.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for ICT Tools in Communication.

   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after ICT Tools in Communication.

6. When learning Introduction to Materials, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)

8. When learning Free-hand sketching, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Free-hand sketching.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Free-hand sketching.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Free-hand sketching.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Free-hand sketching.

9. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. International Cricket Team
   B. Input Cable Tester
   C. Internal Cooking Timer
   D. Information and Communication Technology

10. When learning Introduction to Drawing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Drawing.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Introduction to Drawing.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Introduction to Drawing.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Introduction to Drawing.

15. When learning Measuring and Marking Out Tools, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
